question: Should Discord component callbacks default to 7 days and allow a 30-day `agentComponents.ttlMs` maximum, or should the default/ceiling stay shorter or opt-in?
rationale: The code path is narrow, but the default changes existing upgrade behavior and the max changes the stale-action exposure window; automation cannot choose that product/security tradeoff.

options.title: Accept after reference fix
options.body: Update the stale public config reference and land the PR if maintainers want async Discord review cards to work by default across a weekly cycle.

options.title: Keep shorter default
options.body: Preserve the 30-minute default and require deployments to opt into longer callback windows through the existing config field.

options.title: Revise the ceiling
options.body: Keep a longer default or opt-in path but choose a lower maximum than 30 days and align schema, docs, metadata, and tests.

recommendation.title: Accept after reference fix
recommendation.body: Update the stale public config reference and land the PR if maintainers want async Discord review cards to work by default across a weekly cycle.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior TTL config PR and have recent adjacent Discord/config/docs ownership signals for this policy choice.
